system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",

 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

response: {"headline": "AIM-HIGH (3,414 patients) was stopped early for futility after the DSMB found less than a 1 in 10,000 chance of ever showing significant benefit; the trial's explicit hypothesis — incremental benefit from raising HDL-C on top of statin therapy — was doomed because HDL-C is not causal for coronary artery disease.", "summary": "The AIM-HIGH trial randomized 3,414 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and optimally treated LDL-C (baseline 71 mg/dL on simvastatin) to extended-release niacin or placebo, with baseline HDL-C of 34.9 mg/dL and triglycerides of 161 mg/dL. The primary endpoint was a composite of coronary heart disease death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, hospitalization for acute coronary syndrome, or symptom-driven coronary or cerebral revascularization. The trial was designed for 850 events with 85% power to detect a 25% relative risk reduction based on HDL-C raising, but it was stopped early on 2011-05-26 because the DSMB judged the chance of eventual benefit to be less than 1 in 10,000. The calculator estimates an expected hazard ratio of 0.928 (7.2% RRR) based on LDL-C lowering of 0.338 mmol/L (from -18.4% on baseline 1.836 mmol/L), yielding only 19.2% power against a minimum detectable HR of 0.825 for 80% power. The primary explanation is biomarker_not_causal: the intended biomarker (HDL-C) is non-causal for coronary artery disease, and the trial's explicit rationale was to test incremental benefit from raising HDL-C.
